Execute VectorVM random opcode0x22 using the actual shared native CRT RNG.

Parameters: pContext (RCX) is the VM execution context. Verified fields are +00 bytecode cursor, +08 float-register pointer table, +10 constant-byte buffer and +38 unsigned instance count. No complete context struct is inferred.
Returns: void; both operand modes converge on RET141B11974.

Algorithm:
Read a mode byte and two big-endian 16-bit operands. Mode0 selects an input register and output register. Mode1 selects a constant byte offset and output register. Both advance the bytecode cursor by5. Other mode bytes consume only the mode byte and perform no draws.
For valid admitted instance counts, execute ceil(count/4) vector batches. Each batch calls IAT14322D800 four times, using the same rand import as MoveVM140366FEE and debris140895D68/1408960FF. Normalize by float14325BCB4 and multiply by the input lane or broadcast constant. The four returned draws are stored in reversed lane order (fourth draw to lane0). Padded lanes also consume draws and receive outputs.

Rollback dependency:
141B126E0 dispatches opcode22 here; Niagara141BB6690 reaches that VM from emitter update141BCCA00. Thus Niagara is not categorically an isolated/purely visual RNG domain. A changed number of processed particle lanes can change the subsequent native thread RNG state. Native141BC8970 emitter initialization separately consumes this import for burst ranges.
This proves the native RNG dependency, not the presence of an active Niagara system in the qualification match or a specific pose-to-population effect. Preserve actual draws/order; do not replace with a count from expected history.

The exported variable inventory exposes only the RCX parameter and saved-register/stack artifacts. Register-only decoder, sample and loop variables retain decompiler names; their types follow byte decoding, SSE scalar floats and unsigned batch arithmetic. Saved SIMD/stack placeholders are not modeled as logical locals. The supported count bound must exclude unsigned count+3 overflow.
